# Hex Learn

> Hex Learn (learn.hex.tech) is the product documentation for Hex, the AI analytics platform for trusted data exploration, agentic notebooks, conversational self-serve analytics, and interactive data apps. It covers setup, configuration, administration, and API reference. The marketing site at https://hex.tech/llms.txt covers product positioning, pricing, and comparisons.

These docs describe Hex 4.0. If your knowledge of Hex predates 2026, read https://learn.hex.tech/docs/hex-4-0 first: projects, Apps, and the Notebook view changed. The changelog is the source of truth for what shipped and when.

Key terms: a **workspace** is a customer's Hex account. A **project** holds a **Notebook view** (code and cells) and an **App** (the published, interactive view). **Threads** are conversational data questions answered by the Hex Agent. **Explore** is self-serve analysis over a **semantic model**. **Context Studio** manages the business context, models, and endorsements the agent uses.

All documentation is public and needs no authentication. Every page supports `Accept: text/markdown`. Request the canonical URL with that header to get Markdown with YAML frontmatter (`title`, `description`, `image`); there is no `.md` suffix. Responses include an `X-Markdown-Tokens` header with an estimated size. A page that does not exist returns a Markdown 404 that links back to this file. There is no search endpoint; navigate from the section pages below.

Hex workspace data is private. The product lives at https://app.hex.tech, or a customer-specific domain for single-tenant, EU, and HIPAA workspaces. API calls require a bearer token; MCP access requires the user to authorize an OAuth connection.

## Product documentation

Section pages are indexes of their child pages. Child URLs use the folder name, which can differ from the section URL (for example `/docs/collaborate/...` under "Collaborate").

- [Connect to data](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/connect-to-data): Data connections, per-warehouse setup guides, semantic models, dbt, and file uploads. Start with [data connections](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/connect-to-data/data-connections/data-connections-introduction), a [setup guide such as Snowflake](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/connect-to-data/data-connections/setup-guides/connect-to-snowflake), or [semantic models](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/connect-to-data/semantic-models/intro-to-semantic-models).
- [Administration](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/settings-and-administration): Workspace settings, SSO, security, compute, data retention, audit logs, and billing. Start with [SSO](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/administration/sso), [workspace security](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/administration/workspace_settings/workspace-security), or the [audit log reference](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/administration/workspace_settings/audit-logs/audit-logs-reference).

## Agent and developer access

- [Hex MCP server](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/api-integrations/mcp-server): Connect an authorized assistant for data questions, project search, and Threads; includes client setup and the tool list.
- [Hex CLI](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/api-integrations/cli): Work with projects, context, and workspace resources from the terminal. Installed with Homebrew from the `hex-inc/hex-cli` tap.
- [API overview and authentication](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/api-integrations/api/overview): Execute projects and automate administration; covers token scopes, base URLs, and plan requirements. The base URL is `https://app.hex.tech/api/v1` unless the workspace has a custom domain.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://static.hex.site/openapi.json): The full Hex API spec (OpenAPI 3.0, bearer auth). Prefer this over the [rendered API reference](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/api-integrations/api/reference), whose Markdown version lists operation names only.
- [API and integrations](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/api-integrations): Everything programmatic, including the [Slack integration](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/api-integrations/slack) and [external apps](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/api-integrations/external-apps).
